topic: Characterize the optimal dimension-free approximation frontier for selecting at most k pretreatment covariates to tighten the Gaussian conditional-optimal-transport sharp lower bound on mean squared individual treatment effects. In randomized binary-treatment data with unequal Gaussian arm scales, 2k-sparse covariate eigenvalues in [m,M], conditional residual floor σ_min², and outcome-variance ceiling V, derive the angular residual-information identity; prove γ_k≥(m/M)σ_min²/V and the induced greedy guarantee; construct legal unequal-scale families approaching k/[1+(k−1)(M/m)(V/σ_min²)] to establish both-factor sharpness and dimension-free optimality; and give independent-sample inference for the selected endpoint, with a conservative whole-class projection interval at equality. Credit generic greedy and post-selection inference as prior machinery rather than novelty. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The Gaussian endpoint increment is exactly a squared chordal distance between upper-hemisphere lifts of residualized arm-score vectors. A sparse Schur-complement frame bound and a hemisphere Lipschitz inequality give γ_k≥(m/M)σ_min²/V, stronger than the gated constant. A legal p=2k unequal-scale family has ratio tending to k/[1+(k−1)(M/m)(V/σ_min²)], proving both condition factors necessary and the dimension-free certificate optimal as k grows. The supplied p=4 witness, 43,280 randomized positive-denominator checks, derivative finite differences, and high-precision sharpness instances passed. Ji–Lei–Spector already cover generic selection-valid inference, so novelty is restricted to the sharp budget frontier; equality-boundary Wald failure is handled by a conservative moment-projection interval. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Determine whether the sharper fixed-k lower bound k/[1+(k−1)KR] is universal; this optional refinement is not needed for the proved dimension-free result. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the p=4,k=2 family at (K,R)=(1,100),(10,2),(10,100), verify all subset residual floors and the limit 2/(KR+1), then independently check the frame and hemisphere inequalities. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/pid_cot_covbudget_angular_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the sharper fixed-k guarantee k/[1+(k−1)KR], with K=M/m and R=V/σ_min², universal for greedy selection of at most k covariates for the unequal-scale Gaussian conditional-OT lower endpoint?

source_refs.claim: Covariates tighten causal partial-identification intervals through conditional optimal transport, but the paper does not study cardinality-constrained covariate selection.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Introduces the submodularity ratio and bounds greedy subset selection using sparse covariance eigenvalues.
source_refs.author: Abhimanyu Das and David Kempe

source_refs.claim: Gives tight generic cardinality-constrained greedy guarantees in terms of submodularity ratio and generalized curvature.
source_refs.author: Andrew An Bian, Joachim M. Buhmann, Andreas Krause, and Sebastian Tschiatschek

source_refs.claim: Develops inference for quadratic-cost COT and identifies automatic selection of influential covariates as a future direction.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic weak-submodularity theory yields guarantees from a lower bound on the submodularity ratio, but it does not exploit the coupled Gaussian residual-scale geometry imposed by a causal COT endpoint. Conversely, the COT literature establishes bound tightening and estimation without a cardinality budget. Targeted searches found no work joining these strands. The unresolved step is whether Schur-complement and hemisphere geometry constrain every legal Gaussian set function enough to yield the fixed-k rational expression, or whether some legal covariance construction violates it.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem proving inf F(S_greedy)/max_{|S|≤k}F(S)=k/[1+(k−1)KR] over the stated Gaussian model class, together with attaining unequal-scale covariance families, or a legal counterexample and the corrected sharp fixed-k formula.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from wide causal bounds to covariate-assisted COT; the cardinality-budget obstruction can be introduced at that point.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Joint potential outcomes are unobserved -> COT gives sharp causal bounds -> covariates tighten those bounds -> a cardinality budget demands a sharp approximation frontier

method_exemplars.technique: Translate sparse eigenvalue control into a lower submodularity ratio, then telescope greedy marginal gains against the optimal support.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint improvement is a covariance-driven set function with the same sparse-spectral skeleton, augmented by two-arm transport geometry.

method_exemplars.technique: Refine greedy analysis jointly through submodularity ratio and curvature and construct matching extremal set functions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sharper fixed-k ratio requires either an additional structural parameter or proof that Gaussian COT geometry enforces special curvature.

method_exemplars.technique: Use held-out or multiplier-bootstrap evaluation of dual-bound scores to retain validity after choosing covariates or nuisance models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies established inference machinery for the selected causal endpoint without making generic post-selection validity part of the frontier's novelty.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one select at most k covariates for smooth-density conditional OT to minimize endpoint mean-squared error while accounting simultaneously for population bound tightening and the dimension-dependent wavelet estimation rate?

source_refs.claim: COT estimation suffers a covariate-dimensionality curse; the paper obtains a wavelet CLT under smoothness and names automatic influential-covariate selection as future work.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Provides uniformly valid COT-dual inference and multiplier-bootstrap model or covariate selection, but does not characterize an MSE-optimal cardinality budget.
source_refs.author: Wenlong Ji, Lihua Lei, and Asher Spector

source_refs.claim: A direct adapted-Wasserstein estimator is consistent but has dimension-dependent convergence, making inclusion of every available covariate statistically costly.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adding covariates monotonically tightens the population identified set but increases the dimension governing nonparametric COT error. Existing COT papers analyze fixed conditioning sets, while selection-valid inference does not provide an oracle characterization of this tightening-versus-estimation tradeoff. The first proof step that changes is the fixed-dimension wavelet stability expansion: selection changes both the COT functional and its smoothing resolution, so a post-selection wrapper alone cannot establish MSE-optimality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit data-driven size-k selector with an oracle inequality for squared error of the selected COT endpoint and a uniform limit law or confidence interval attaining the oracle rate over a stated smoothness class.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames covariate dimension as the obstacle to COT inference and directly identifies automatic influential-covariate selection as future work.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Covariates tighten COT bounds -> nonparametric COT deteriorates with dimension -> smoothness restores inference for a fixed set -> budgeted selection must optimize tightening against estimation error

method_exemplars.technique: Wavelet density projection, marginal alignment, quadratic-cost stability, and asymptotic linearization of the COT value.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired oracle risk must explicitly incorporate this estimator's dimension-dependent bias and variance.

method_exemplars.technique: Multiplier-bootstrap comparison of candidate covariate models using uniformly valid dual-bound scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles validity under model selection; the missing addition is a size-k oracle-risk result tied to endpoint MSE.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert restricted curvature of a continuous objective into weak submodularity of its support-restricted value function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A tractable selector would follow if population tightening or negative endpoint risk admitted a restricted-curvature certificate.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the shortest uniformly honest confidence interval for the greedy-selected Gaussian COT lower endpoint along local sequences where the treated and control residual-score lifts coincide and the endpoint increment is zero?

source_refs.claim: Establishes uniformly valid inference and multiplier-bootstrap selection for covariate-assisted partial-identification bounds.
source_refs.author: Wenlong Ji, Lihua Lei, and Asher Spector

source_refs.claim: Shows that confidence-interval coverage can fail to be uniform as an identified interval approaches point identification and gives a Gaussian correction.
source_refs.author: Guido W. Imbens and Charles F. Manski

source_refs.claim: Constructs a short, never-empty interval for parameters with asymptotically normal estimated lower and upper bounds.
source_refs.author: Jörg Stoye

source_refs.claim: Proves asymptotic normality for a fixed quadratic-cost COT endpoint under smooth densities, without analyzing a selected zero-increment boundary.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Generic selection-valid procedures provide conservative coverage, so validity alone is not the gap. At equality, the Gaussian endpoint is locally a squared norm or chordal distance with vanishing first derivative, while the selected subset is unstable under root-n perturbations. The regular Wald law therefore degenerates exactly where the active model can switch. Existing partial-identification work treats collapsing intervals and COT work treats fixed-functional CLTs, but neither supplies a local minimax length characterization for this selected quadratic boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A local asymptotic experiment for root-n perturbations of the residual-score difference, an honest whole-class interval with uniform coverage through equality, and a matching lower bound on expected length or an optimality theorem within projection intervals.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates why inference must remain uniform as a partially identified region collapses, matching the boundary encountered when the COT gain vanishes.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Bound endpoints are estimable -> ordinary intervals work away from collapse -> coverage becomes nonuniform near equality -> the selected Gaussian COT endpoint needs boundary-uniform, length-aware inference

method_exemplars.technique: Selection-valid multiplier bootstrap for maxima over candidate covariate and model scores.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It handles the random selected model, leaving the quadratic zero-derivative boundary and length optimality as the new steps.

method_exemplars.technique: Calibrate critical values uniformly over shrinking identified-set width in a Gaussian limit experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Equality of residual lifts is analogous to a vanishing identification-region width.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine an identified-set interval with a pseudotrue-parameter interval to obtain short, never-empty coverage.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its length-conscious construction is a benchmark for a conservative whole-class projection interval at equality.

open_problems.open_problem: Does the Gaussian dimension-free covariate-budget frontier extend to conditionally elliptical treatment arms with a common radial generator, and if not, what generator-dependent constant replaces the Gaussian frontier?

source_refs.claim: Derives the closed-form W2 formula for elliptically contoured families and the covariance-based lower bound now called the Gelbrich bound.
source_refs.author: Matthias Gelbrich

source_refs.claim: Studies W2 geometry for elliptical distributions with common density generators and implications for equality in the Gelbrich bound.
source_refs.author: Song Fang and Quanyan Zhu

source_refs.claim: Frames covariate-assisted causal bounds as COT values for general outcome laws, without a sparse-selection approximation frontier.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

open_problems.why_unsolved: Unconditional W2 geometry agrees with the Gaussian covariance formula for elliptical laws sharing a generator, suggesting a transfer route. Conditioning an elliptical vector on different covariate subsets, however, generally changes its radial generator and may make the generator depend on the conditioning value. The first Gaussian proof step—the exact squared-chordal identity for an endpoint increment—therefore need not survive, and targeted searches found no elliptical conditional-OT result combined with sparse greedy covariate selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem giving the sharp dimension-free greedy ratio over a specified common-generator conditional-elliptical class, with a generator-dependent constant and extremizers, or a counterexample showing that no positive dimension-free constant follows from K and R alone.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the causal-bound and COT motivation, while the elliptical restriction can be introduced explicitly as the destination model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Causal heterogeneity is partially identified -> covariates sharpen COT bounds -> Gaussian geometry yields tractable budget guarantees -> elliptical arms test whether the guarantee is distributional or merely Gaussian

method_exemplars.technique: Represent W2 through means and covariance square roots for common-generator elliptical distributions and use the Gelbrich inequality outside equality cases.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This directly tests whether residualized elliptical arm distances retain the Gaussian angular representation.

method_exemplars.technique: Control aggregate marginal gains by sparse covariance eigenvalues and telescope the greedy recursion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: If the elliptical endpoint increment admits a covariance-based lower comparison, the remaining budget argument has the same sparse-frame structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Quadratic COT stability and asymptotic linearization under smooth densities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An elliptical identification frontier admits an estimation rung, and this supplies limit theory for the corresponding fixed-subset endpoint.

open_problems.open_problem: How well does greedy covariate selection based only on the Gaussian/Gelbrich endpoint approximate the true quadratic conditional-OT lower bound over non-elliptical arm distributions with the same sparse-covariance and residual-floor restrictions?

source_refs.claim: The covariance expression is a universal W2 lower bound and is exact only for special elliptical families.
source_refs.author: Matthias Gelbrich

source_refs.claim: Conditional OT gives covariate-assisted causal bounds for general distributions, while its practical method approximates the full conditional problem.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

source_refs.claim: Shows that direct empirical COT is unstable under weak convergence and develops adapted-Wasserstein estimation for the true COT value.
source_refs.author: Sirui Lin, Zijun Gao, Jose Blanchet, and Peter Glynn

open_problems.why_unsolved: The Gaussian selector optimizes a second-moment surrogate. Gelbrich's inequality places that surrogate below the true quadratic transport cost but does not compare marginal gains across conditioning sets, so a subset maximizing surrogate tightening may perform poorly for true COT tightening. Sparse eigenvalues and residual floors constrain only second moments and may leave higher-order shape changes unrestricted. Targeted searches found no approximation or impossibility theorem linking Gelbrich-surrogate selection to true conditional OT.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp multiplicative or additive sandwich between the true COT gain of the Gaussian-surrogate greedy subset and the optimal size-k true-COT gain under an explicit distributional regularity class, or a moment-matched family proving that no nonzero guarantee follows from K and R alone.

writing_exemplar.why: Its general-distribution COT formulation shows why a cheap Gaussian surrogate is attractive and why fidelity to the causal bound matters.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: True causal bounds require conditional OT -> full COT is statistically and computationally difficult -> Gaussian moment geometry offers a cheap selector -> its approximation to true bound tightening needs a sharp robustness certificate

method_exemplars.technique: Lower-bound W2 by the Bures/Gelbrich covariance expression and characterize equality for structured distribution families.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired comparison begins by decomposing true COT gain into the Gaussian surrogate plus a non-ellipticity slack.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate the true COT functional using adapted-Wasserstein topology and derive its convergence rate.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a way to estimate and validate the destination quantity rather than only its moment surrogate.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct uniformly valid dual-bound scores around conditional-distribution estimates and use multiplier selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supports inference after surrogate-based subset selection even when the Gaussian conditional model is misspecified.

literature_map:
Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn (ICML 2025, arXiv:2502.01164) formulate covariate-assisted causal partial identification through conditional OT and a tractable relaxation.
Ji, Lei, and Spector (arXiv:2310.08115) give model-agnostic, uniformly valid dual-bound inference and multiplier-bootstrap covariate/model selection.
Lin et al. (AISTATS 2026, arXiv:2506.00257) show direct plug-in COT is inconsistent under weak topology and use adapted-Wasserstein continuity for consistent estimation.
Lin et al. (arXiv:2602.20681) obtain quadratic-COT stability and a smooth-density wavelet CLT while explicitly pointing to automatic influential-covariate selection as future work.
Aronow, Green, and Lee (Annals of Statistics 2014, arXiv:1405.6555) establish sharp variance bounds in randomized experiments from marginal outcome laws.
Wang, Wang, Miao, and Zhou (Statistica Sinica 2024, arXiv:2011.09829) add covariates to sharp finite-population variance bounds and uniformly conservative inference.
Das and Kempe (ICML 2011, arXiv:1102.3975) introduce the submodularity ratio and sparse-eigenvalue greedy analysis for regression subset selection.
Elenberg, Khanna, Dimakis, and Negahban (Annals of Statistics 2018, DOI:10.1214/17-AOS1679) derive weak submodularity from restricted curvature.
Bian et al. (ICML 2017, arXiv:1703.02100) give tight generic greedy guarantees combining submodularity ratio and curvature.
The COT and weak-submodularity strands remain separate: targeted searches found no cardinality-budget frontier for covariate-assisted causal OT bounds.
Gelbrich (Mathematische Nachrichten 1990, DOI:10.1002/mana.19901470121) gives the covariance W2 bound and elliptical equality structure, exposing both an extension route and a misspecification gap.
Imbens and Manski (Econometrica 2004) show why inference must be uniform as an identified interval collapses; Stoye (2021) supplies a short, never-empty interval benchmark.
The main live tension is population monotonicity—more covariates tighten the identified set—versus statistical deterioration as conditional-distribution dimension grows.
The strongest topic-specific gap is whether legal unequal-scale Gaussian COT objectives force the sharper fixed-k ratio k/[1+(k−1)KR], beyond generic weak-submodular guarantees.
